text:
sara: :rotating_light: paging oncall - we're seeing p95/p99 spikes for pool-dedicated-nyc-2 (customer: AcmeCorp) starting ~11:05 UTC. Streaming sessions are stalling, a bunch of clients hit inactivity timeouts. Error rate up ~3x.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-78, severity: high. Notifying oncall.

oncall-rosa: I'm on it. quick status? which metrics are spiking?

sara: p95 went from 80ms to 1.2s, p99 ~6.3s. Queue depth for pool-dedicated-nyc-2 jumped from baseline ~20 to 480. Autoscaler logs show multiple failed handshakes with the warmup service during the burst.

ajay: grabbing autoscaler and warmup logs now. last successful scale event was 10:58 UTC, then heavy burst at 11:04. Warmup handshake times are 12-18s per node which exceeds handshake timeout (10s) causing node rejects.

maria: that's the handshake timeout we lowered last week for faster rollbacks. Did we also change the prewarm window?

sara: yes, config: `autoscale.handshake_timeout=10s`, `autoscale.prewarm_target=2` (we reduced to lower idle). Looks like in a sustained burst that prewarm is too low.

ajay: pasting clipped logs:
```
[11:05:12] autoscaler: requestScale(pool=pool-dedicated-nyc-2, delta=8)
[11:05:12] warmup: handshake start id=abcd123
[11:05:25] warmup: handshake timeout id=abcd123 error=timeout waiting for kv-init
[11:05:25] autoscaler: scaleRejected pool=pool-dedicated-nyc-2 reason=handshake_timeout
```

oncall-rosa: Oof. That `kv-init` hang is familiar — seen this with recent kernel upgrade on warmup images. Any node-level logs?

ajay: node logs show `kv-cache: cold_path_fetch=1.8s` on initial warmups. Memory pressure and slow nvme reads on the new instance SKU.

support-rob: AcmeCorp support ticket (#AC-4392) is filling up with timed-out streaming sessions; they reported degraded interactive generation around 11:07 UTC. We should assess customer impact and whether to notify them.

sara: agreed. I'll prepare an initial customer-facing note: "We're investigating increased latency and streaming stalls in NYC region affecting dedicated pools. We're implementing mitigations and will follow up with ETA."

maria: Mitigation options: 1) Temporarily raise `prewarm_target` to 6 for pool-dedicated-nyc-2 to reduce cold handshakes. 2) Increase `handshake_timeout` to 30s to allow kv-init. 3) Create routing rule to divert new streaming sessions to a hosted fallback model/region for AcmeCorp. 4) Rollback the warmup image/kernel change if it correlates. Which to do first?

oncall-rosa: Do 2) + 1) immediately (safest). Then 3) if we still see failures.

ajay: executing change now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/pools/pool-dedicated-nyc-2/config -d '{"autoscale.prewarm_target":6, "autoscale.handshake_timeout":"30s"}'` — applying.

deploy-bot: config update queued. patch-id=cfg-nyc-0423-9. Rolling update to pool control plane.

11:12:40 deploy-bot: config applied successfully to pool-dedicated-nyc-2.

sara: after change, queue depth dropping: 480 -> 190 over 4m. p95 trending down to ~320ms. p99 still elevated ~2.1s. Streaming stalls reduced but not resolved.

ajay: still seeing a handful of rejected handshakes, but much fewer. Node-level KV cold path still ~1.2s on a few instances. Suggest we spin up one extra warmup replica class with higher io throughput to soak cold paths while we triage kernel/AMI.

maria: agreed. I'll request a targeted capacity bump: `reserve-add --pool pool-dedicated-nyc-2 --count 4 --sku io-optimized` (manual slot request).

support-rob: recommending we send an update to AcmeCorp: short note about mitigations (config changes + routing fallback if needed) and estimated next update in 30m. Want to avoid SLA language until we confirm.

sara: drafting message: "We saw an autoscaling handshake regression causing delayed warmups and streaming stalls for your dedicated pool in NYC. We've increased prewarm capacity and handshake timeout which has improved latency; we're provisioning additional warmup capacity and investigating the warmup image. Next update in 30m or sooner." Agree?

oncall-rosa: LGTM. send from support alias and cc eng-sre.

ajay: kicked off AMI revert test and will run warmup health checks against the previous image. Command I ran:
```
# quick smoke warmup against previous image
warmup-run --image ami-20260401-prev --pool pool-dedicated-nyc-2 --test-only
```

11:28:01 incident-bot: Paging update: mitigation in progress. Latency improving; customer impact reduced to partial.

maria: note for postmortem: root cause candidates = 1) recent warmup image/kernel causing slow nvme reads on some SKUs, 2) aggressive handshake timeout + low prewarm target, 3) autoscaler backoff logic that retries too slowly under burst. We'll need histogram traces and handshake timing correlations.

ajay: collecting traces and will dump the handshake histograms to the incident channel. Also tagging the autoscaler team.

sara: next steps: - keep current config for 1 hour while monitoring - provision io-optimized warmup replicas - run AMI revert test and if green, roll warmup fleet back - prepare postmortem template with customer impact numbers (p95/p99 baseline vs incident, total timed-out streams).

support-rob: customer update sent at 11:30 UTC. They acknowledged and appreciate rapid response.

oncall-rosa: I'm going to stay on this for the next hour and hand off at 12:45 UTC unless escalation needed. If p99 > 3s or queue depth > 250 re-escalate paging.

sara: thanks everyone. adding playbook items to the incident ticket and will kick off postmortem once stable. :white_check_mark:

ajay: attaching quick graph links: https://graf.redwood/pool-dedicated-nyc-2/handshake-histo && https://graf.redwood/pool-dedicated-nyc-2/queue-depth

maria: jotting down follow-ups: audit recent kernel/AMI change, add warmup image canary test, revisit default `handshake_timeout` and tie it to kv-init latency percentiles, add automated temporary prewarm ramp when queue depth delta > X.

11:33:40 incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, impact reduced. Monitoring until fully resolved.

sara: closing note: if anyone observes a regression or sees the ticket pop in customer Slack, ping me directly. Good catch.

11:37:00 last-ack: oncall-rosa acknowledged and will remain on duty until handoff.
